intro: Studio City runs along Ventura Boulevard at the foot of the Santa Monica Mountains, with the CBS studio lot, a long strip of sushi bars and neighborhood restaurants, a classic jazz club on Cahuenga and trailheads like Fryman Canyon a few minutes up the hill.

gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites Nathaniel checked)

places.w: A busy neighborhood coffee shop with well-balanced espresso drinks and good pastries.
places.o: An iced vanilla latte and a cinnamon roll.

places.w: An all-day neighborhood cafe where the pastry case and sandwiches draw a steady line.
places.o: Coffee and something from the bakery case.

places.w: Sonoran-style tacos on fresh flour tortillas, with meats cooked over mesquite.
places.o: The thin-cut ribeye taco.

places.w: A tiny counter near the studios turning out kabobs, shawarma and falafel wraps.
places.o: A falafel laffa or the beef kabob plate.

places.w: A quick counter built around spit-roasted shawarma.
places.o: The wagyu shawarma sandwich.

places.w: One of the strongest ramen shops in the Valley, with big bowls worth taking home.
places.o: The spicy Reddo, plus the brothless Orenji to share.

places.w: A cluttered, homey Japanese comfort food spot tucked into a strip mall.
places.o: The original poke bowl.

places.w: A Northern Thai specialist known for its rich curry noodle soup.
places.o: Khao soi with crispy pork or soft-shell crab.

places.w: A family-run Armenian restaurant with generous plates and a warm room.
places.o: The mantee dumplings with yogurt, dolma and the sizzling feta.

places.w: A long-running gastropub under a brick barrel ceiling with a big shareable menu that works for groups.
places.o: Small plates to share and a cocktail.

places.w: A friendly neighborhood bar with a solid happy hour.
places.o: The burger and a beer.

places.w: A casual pasta bar making fresh pasta in a relaxed setting.
places.o: Two pastas to share.

places.w: An Italian dining room pairing raw seafood with pastas and a good wine list. Dinner only, closed Mondays.
places.o: Oysters and a couple of crudos to start.

places.w: A dark, moody Argentine steakhouse built around an open fire grill.
places.o: Piquillo peppers and the lamb saddle. It is a splurge.

places.w: An old-school sushi bar on Ventura's sushi row, known for pristine nigiri.
places.o: The omakase if you want the full tour of their signatures.

places.w: A neighborhood sushi bar where ordering nigiri at the counter is the move.
places.o: Sit at the bar, order a la carte and get the hirame.

places.w: A good-value sushi spot that does especially well as takeout.
places.o: The Yume Box.

places.w: A post-apocalyptic themed cocktail bar with fully committed decor and a real kitchen.
places.o: A house cocktail and a few shared plates.

places.w: A small, long-running jazz club where the menu is giant stuffed baked potatoes.
places.o: Buy tickets online ahead of time, since shows sell out.

places.w: A shady canyon loop with a steady climb and Valley views, popular with dog walkers.
places.o: Go early; the lot fills fast on weekends.

places.w: A candlelit restaurant and lounge with a library bar and heated patios with fireplaces. The Valley's dress-up night out, busy until late.
places.o: Drinks in the library, then dinner on the patio. Book ahead on weekends.
